work_order.confidence_rationale: All four findings were re-checked on current main (779a660) before planning and all four still hold. The suite is 297 pass / 0 fail there, run directly this session (the first run read 7 files as failing only because node_modules was absent; `npm ci` restores 297/0), so nothing since #66 has fixed any of them. The read-side widening was measured end-to-end against a booted app: a 'ZZZ' row reads metrics 7_200_000_000 / CPL 2_400_000_000 and a ₹2,400.00 tile while POSTing one more rupee to that same tenant returns 400. This version changes one step of the previous plan in response to the plan review. I re-verified that objection first-hand rather than taking it on trust: rendering all 25 page x state combinations on a freshly seeded INR database with a Meta provider attached gives a Qualified CPL tile of ₹2,400.00 on `/` at ?state=ideal and ?state=partial (7 rupee amounts each) and on `/?meta_error=quota` and `/?meta_error=revoked` (7 each), zero amounts and no tile on `/` at ?state=empty, ?state=loading and ?state=error, and no Qualified CPL tile on /journal, /opportunities, /experiments or /approvals in any state (amount counts 0 / 6 / 4 / 0). The old step 11 asserted a tile and rupee amounts on shells that render neither, so it could not be executed as written on a correct build. It is rewritten below, keeping all five states and all five pages. The residual is a fixture detail in the new tests, not the behaviour: the only case that changes at all is a stored code naming no currency.
work_order.understanding:
Four non-blocking findings the reviewer of #66 approved despite, filed as it merged. I re-checked all four against current main (779a660) before planning; the suite is 297 pass / 0 fail there (run directly this session), not the 294 the finding text quotes, so nothing since has fixed any of them. They are one root cause in one place — a tenant row's stored currency being resolved differently by each helper that reads it — and they ship as one change. Splitting them would put the two halves of the read-side fix (routes.js and pages.js) in separate PRs, and the dashboard and the API are asserted to agree, so a half-applied fix fails a test that is already in the suite.

FINDING 1 (src/api/routes.js:72) is a real behaviour regression on the read side and the reason the other three are here. #66 moved the INR fallback off the write path but left it on the read path, where it now changes a money-bearing API number rather than a rendering. Measured end to end on a booted app, on a fresh DB with one INR spend of 7_200_000_000 and three qualified leads, then the tenant row held at 'ZZZ' by the same raw SQL the QA repro uses: GET /v1/metrics?tenant_id=tenant_demo returns {"spend_micros":7200000000,"qualified_volume":3,"qualified_cpl_micros":2400000000} and the dashboard Qualified CPL tile reads ₹2,400.00 — while POSTing one more INR spend to that same tenant returns 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH. The row is held at a code naming no currency, the write path refuses to add a rupee to it, and the read reports rupees it holds. On ed5aa90 the same database read {"spend_micros":0,…,"qualified_cpl_micros":null} and the tile read the em-dash; #63 (4372b06) introduced the widening, and this PR inherits it. The dashboard inherits the same line through pages.js:213, which feeds computeFunnel at pages.js:414.

FINDING 2 (src/api/routes.js:87) and FINDING 4 (the same two lines) are the same edit, and the second is the one I am taking. tenantCurrencyMismatch null-guards the row for the canonical read and dereferences it for the verbatim read, so a null row throws TypeError instead of answering — I reproduced that — while resolveTenantCurrency on the same shape returns 'INR'. Written as a coalesce it is one rule rather than two arms with different left operands, and it is one character shorter with the misleading `?.` gone. I checked the coalesce against the ternary over every shape that reaches the helper ('ZZZ', 'usd', ' USD ', 'INR', 'x', '') against three spend currencies: identical results on all eighteen. No call site can pass a null row today — the sole call site is guarded by `existingTenant &&` on the same line — so dropping the `?.` states a precondition the call site already makes rather than half-honouring one that cannot arrive.

FINDING 3 (src/web/pages.js:241) is right that the comment overstates, and the read-side fix makes the comment's claim not merely overstated but inverted, so it must be replaced rather than narrowed. The comment says money()'s membership guard cannot be pinned by a test because no current caller can reach it. After this ticket, a 'ZZZ' tenant reaches it on every money() call on every screen, and it is load-bearing: without it fromMicros(6_000_000_000, 'ZZZ') throws INVALID_CURRENCY and the page 500s, which is precisely the outcome that comment says the guard exists to prevent. test/web/pages.test.js:1171 already renders a 'ZZZ' tenant and asserts the rupee relabelling, so the guard is covered, not invisible.
work_order.root_cause: One stored currency, four questions, and no single answer to 'what does a code that names no currency mean'. #63 introduced resolveTenantCurrency's `canonicalCurrency(stored) ?? 'INR'` on the read side; #66 introduced tenantCurrencyMismatch for the write side and left the read alone. The two now disagree on purpose for one row, and the read is the side that reports numbers: the read guesses INR for a row the write path will refuse to add to. The same split is mirrored in pages.js:213 and routes.js:88, where the optional chain and the ternary both describe one rule as two.
work_order.approach:
Give the read side the same treatment the write side already got: a stored code that names an ISO currency is canonicalised, a stored code that names none is passed through VERBATIM so it matches no spend row, and INR is a fallback for a MISSING row only. Three lines of source, plus the comment text the change makes false.

The rule, stated once, for every call site of both seams:
  canonical currency -> that code ('usd', ' USD ' -> 'USD')
  a code naming no currency -> VERBATIM ('ZZZ' stays 'ZZZ', '' stays '')
  a missing tenant row -> 'INR'
The invariant: for a tenant whose stored code names no currency, the read reports no spend and a null CPL, because that code matches no stored spend row — and the write path 400s a spend against it, so the two surfaces now agree about what the row is instead of one guessing rupees and the other refusing them.

Worked examples, computed by driving the real computeFunnel and money() on this tree, over a tenant holding one INR spend of 7_200_000_000 and three qualified leads (values are spend_micros / qualified_cpl_micros):
  stored 'ZZZ'  -> before 7_200_000_000 / 2_400_000_000, after 0 / null          (the change)
  stored ''     -> before 7_200_000_000 / 2_400_000_000, after 0 / null          (same rule, see below)
  stored 'usd'  -> 0 / null before and after                                     (unchanged)
  stored ' USD '-> 0 / null before and after                                     (unchanged)
  stored 'INR'  -> 7_200_000_000 / 2_400_000_000 before and after               (unchanged)
  stored 'USD'  -> 0 / null before and after                                     (unchanged)
  no tenant row -> 0 / null before and after                                     (unchanged)
Only the two rows naming no currency move, and they move from a wrong-unit number to an honest unknown. qualified_volume is 3 in every row: computeFunnel filters spend rows only (src/domain/measurement.js:191-208), so a volume survives a currency the spend side cannot name. Any input: the sum of the excluded rows is the sum the funnel reports, so spend_micros is 0 whenever the stored code names no currency, and qualified_cpl_micros is null whenever spend_micros is 0 — never a 0, because a zero CPL would claim free acquisitions.

Implementation note the implementer must not get wrong: the chain is `??`, not `||`. tenants.currency is `TEXT NOT NULL` (src/data/db.js:24), so a present row always holds a string, and `||` would turn a stored '' into INR on the read while tenantCurrencyMismatch still 400s a spend against '' — the exact collapse this change removes. The last `?? 'INR'` covers a MISSING row only, and it must stay: dropping it yields `undefined` for a tenant with no row, and computeFunnel skips currency filtering entirely when tenantCurrency is undefined (measurement.js:201), so a missing row would silently stop excluding foreign legacy rows.

All eight money() call sites in pages.js go through the shared tenantCurrency() seam (363, 383, 414, 427, 781, 795, 870, 886) and I checked each: with the guard in money() intact, the seven non-funnel ones render exactly what they render today ('ZZZ' and '' both relabel to the repo default, and no raw code reaches a reader, because ISO_CURRENCIES.includes() fails and the fallback fires). Only the Qualified CPL tile at 427 changes, because the funnel is the only consumer that compares codes. The seam stays in each file rather than moving to a shared export: both files already carry a private per-file currency seam and the file's own pattern, and a new public domain export is a larger change than the three lines it would save.

Nothing outside src/ and test/ changes. No new dependency, no new route, no new error code, no change to the write path's behaviour, and no new host.

Widen past the script — the breadth sweep, scoped to what each surface actually renders. This change touches one line on each of two surfaces, so the risk is a caller nobody enumerated; the point of the step is breadth, so run all five states on all five pages. Expected counts below were measured on a freshly seeded INR database with a Meta provider attached, and a surface rendering a different number of amounts is worth a look, not an automatic failure. (a) Surfaces that DO render the tile and amounts — load / at ?state=ideal, / at ?state=partial, / at ?meta_error=quota and / at ?meta_error=revoked, and on each assert the Qualified CPL tile reads ₹2,400.00 and that every rendered amount carries the rupee symbol (7 rupee amounts on each of these four on a seeded DB). (b) Surfaces that deliberately render NO amounts — / at ?state=empty, ?state=loading and ?state=error. These three are forced shells with no kpi-strip, no tables and no amounts at all (0 rupee amounts, no Qualified CPL tile), so 'every amount carries the rupee symbol' is vacuously true there rather than failing. Assert the shell each one is documented to render instead: ?state=empty shows the 'No connected ad account yet' checklist with data-testid="dashboard-empty"; ?state=loading shows the skeleton stack (div.skeleton-stack) and no .kpi-value; ?state=error shows the provider-sync error panel with its retry control (data-action="retry"). Do NOT report a missing tile or a missing rupee amount on these three as a failure — a tile there would be the defect. (c) Surfaces with amounts but no tile — /journal, /opportunities, /experiments and /approvals, at each of the five states. None of these four pages has a Qualified CPL tile in any state, so drop the tile assertion entirely and check only the symbol rule: no 'NaN', no 'undefined', no bare micros integer, and every amount carries a currency symbol where the page renders amounts at all (on a seeded INR database /opportunities renders 6 such amounts and /experiments 4; /journal and /approvals render none in any state, so for those two the check is that they render no NaN, no undefined and no raw micros figure — not that an amount is present).
risks: The merged #66 run pinned the opposite of this ticket: its AC-1 and AC-4 and qa_script step 4 asserted that a 'ZZZ' row reads 7_200_000_000 and the tile reads ₹2,400.00, and called that the 'unchanged' baseline. This ticket deliberately reverses that pin. Anyone reading the #66 QA trail without this issue in hand will read the new 0 / null / '—' as a regression, so say so in the PR description.

money()'s membership guard becomes load-bearing rather than decorative. Today tenantCurrency() hides a bad code from it by resolving to INR; after this change every render for such a tenant reaches it, and without it fromMicros throws INVALID_CURRENCY and the page 500s. The guard stays and AC-6 pins it, but the next reader should know that line is now what stands between a bad row and a 500 on every screen.

A tenant row holding '' or any other non-ISO code now reads spend 0 and a null CPL where it read an INR number. That is the intended honest unknown and it matches what the write path has always done, but it is a visible change for any operator whose row is already bad, and the first time they see it they will read it as lost spend. Named in the PR description rather than left to be discovered.

The pages.js change moves one seam that eight money() call sites share. I enumerated all eight (363, 383, 414, 427, 781, 795, 870, 886) and only 427's input changes, but the sweep step in qa_script is there because a caller I did not read is the failure mode this kind of change has.

The final qa_script step is breadth, and breadth steps are where a QA agent is most likely to invent an assertion. It is written surface-by-surface precisely because the previous version of it asserted a Qualified CPL tile and rupee amounts on shells that render neither, which no correct build can satisfy. If a count differs from the expected number given, read the page before reporting: the acceptance criteria are the four numbered ones above, and this step exists to surface a caller nobody enumerated, not to add new criteria.

No path in forbidden_paths is touched (.sdlc/**, .github/**, docs/spec/**, docs/prd.md, docs/trd.md, docs/ui.md are all untouched), and the change adds no host to env.api_allowlist — it reads and writes nothing outside the local SQLite file the app already uses.
out_of_scope: The write path. tenantCurrencyMismatch already answers correctly as merged in #66; this ticket only removes the `?.` that misdescribed it, and changes no 400, no message and no details.

Moving resolveTenantCurrency and tenantCurrency into one shared export in src/domain/money.js. It would shrink the diff by two lines, but it adds a public domain API and restructures two files' own private seams. It would ship on its own; say so and file it separately if you want it.
Returning 404 from GET /v1/metrics for a tenant that has no row. The missing-row INR fallback stays: a read must still answer, and changing that is an API decision, not a bug fix.

Rendering a bad code on screen as 'ZZZ 1,000.00' instead of relabelling it to the repo default. money()'s knowingly-wrong-unit-over-knowingly-unformatted trade is deliberate and unchanged; this ticket only makes the guard that implements it reachable.

Renaming the existing 'ZZZ' render tests at pages.test.js:1171 and :1202. Their titles describe money()'s relabelling fallback, which this ticket does not change; only the funnel's use of the code changes. The implementer is told to leave them alone rather than tidy them, because a rename would obscure that they are the tests now pinning the guard.

The empty string as a distinct bad-data case beyond the `??`-not-`||` guard above — tenants.create takes any string, so '' is reachable through the repository, and it is covered, but making the application reject it at write time is a separate change to that repository.

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep the INR fallback on the read side, record the decision in resolveTenantCurrency's doc comment, and pin it with a test in test/api/events.test.js (the second half of finding 1's fix).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It answers a question nobody asked — what should a bad row draw? — with a guess, and it keeps the read and the write disagreeing about one row: the API would report 7_200_000_000 rupees of spend for a tenant that POST /v1/events 400s a rupee to. The reviewer's own wording for the fallback's justification ('a read must draw something rather than 500') does not hold here: computeFunnel filters and never renders, and the read did not throw or 500 before #63. It is also a number the #66 QA run already pinned as correct, which is how the disagreement survived a review.

alternatives_considered.approach: Fix only src/api/routes.js:203 as finding 1 names, and leave pages.js:213 on the INR fallback.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The two surfaces feed the same computeFunnel from the same row and are asserted to agree — test/web/pages.test.js:377 boots the app and compares both in one test. Fixing one alone inverts the disagreement rather than removing it: the API would read null while the dashboard still showed ₹2,400.00, and that existing test would go red. Half a fix here is not a smaller diff, it is a failing suite.

alternatives_considered.approach: Drop the INR fallback from the read entirely: `canonicalCurrency(stored) ?? stored`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: For a tenant with no row at all that yields `undefined`, and computeFunnel skips currency filtering entirely when tenantCurrency is undefined (measurement.js:201) — so a missing tenant row would silently stop excluding foreign-currency legacy spend, the exact corruption the parameter exists to prevent. The fallback is narrowed to the case it is actually for, not removed.

alternatives_considered.approach: Write the read chain with `||` instead of `??` (`canonicalCurrency(stored) || stored || 'INR'`).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: A stored empty string is falsy, so `||` turns it into INR and the read reports rupees for a row the write side 400s — the same collapse the ticket removes, reintroduced for the one shape `??` distinguishes. The `??`-not-`||` requirement is in the approach, in a test case, and in the qa_script.

alternatives_considered.approach: Split this into four tickets, one per finding.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Findings 2 and 4 are the same two lines, and finding 1's fix is the read half of the same disagreement findings 2 and 4 document. alternatives_considered.approach: Answer the plan review by deleting the breadth sweep from the qa_script, since the only step it objected to was the sweep.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The review asked for the opposite: keep all five states and all five pages, and stop asserting a tile and a rupee amount on shells that render neither. The sweep is the coverage for a caller nobody enumerated, and this change moves a seam shared by eight money() call sites. What was rewritten is the scoping, not the breadth — and the expected counts it now states (7 amounts on the four amount-bearing dashboard shells, 0 on the three forced shells, 6 and 4 on /opportunities and /experiments, 0 on /journal and /approvals) were measured on a seeded INR database so a correct build cannot be reported broken.
